newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Nobel poet laureate Paz escapes blaze.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Nobel poet laureate Paz escapes blaze.

text.p: Nobel poet laureate Octavio Paz escaped unharmed from a blaze that damaged his apartment and destroyed a precious collection of books and artefacts, the author said on Monday.
Firemen said the blaze was caused by a short-circuit in a television set as Paz and his wife slept early on Sunday.

Paz, 82, said they were awakened by an explosion that filled their luxury apartment with thick smoke. The flames engulfed their collection of old books, furniture, carpets and paintings, forcing the couple to abandon the apartment with the help of neighbours.
"Some of the books were inherited from my grandfather," Paz said. "There were paintings and objects given to me as presents over the years, over a lifetime."
TV images showed the charred and blackened remains of the apartment. Oriental stone statues were the only identifiable objects left among the debris.

Paz, who won the Nobel prize for literature in 1990, said hundreds of his books were lost. He suffers from phlebitis, which causes blood circulation problems and restricts his mobility, and local media said he had difficulty getting out of bed and escaping the blaze.
